name: QServe SmoothAttention (4-bit KV cache with an accuracy-preserving correction)
bits: 4-bit KV cache (keys and values), the 'KV4' of W4A8KV4
activation_scheme: Not an activation scheme - 4-bit KV cache mitigated by SmoothAttention, which the paper introduces specifically to counter the accuracy degradation that 4-bit KV quantization causes. The system then makes fused attention memory-bound specifically to capture the KV4 bandwidth win.
kernels: QServe inference library; fused attention kernels made memory-bound to exploit the KV4 reduction.
quality_delta: Throughput figures only in the abstract (LLaMA-3-8B 1.2x on A100 / 1.4x on L40S vs TensorRT-LLM; Qwen1.5-72B 2.4x on A100 / 3.5x on L40S). No KV-specific quality number in the abstract.
notes: Third distinct KV record tied to a weight-quantization paper, and the reason all three are kept separate: QServe's KV contribution is a CORRECTION METHOD (SmoothAttention) rather than a new grouping scheme. That is a genuinely different lever from KIVI's per-channel/per-token axis choice, and it is the one that matters at scale-serving batch sizes where KIVI's low-memory benefit has to coexist with high arithmetic intensity. Note the whole family (KIVI 2/4, KVQuant 3/3, QuaRot 4/4, QServe 4/4, ZipCache mixed) disagrees about the right key bit width - there is no settled answer, and the repo should not imply one by presenting a single record as canonical. SCHEME RECLASSIFIED (parent agent, 2026-10-03): scheme was 'wq4a4' (a proxy recorded while the enum lacked a legal value) and is now 'kv-cache-quant'.
